transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um... I guess I came in because, well, some people have pointed out a few things about how I've been acting, and I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out. 

It's probably nothing too serious, but... they said they can actually see me moving really slowly sometimes. Almost like I'm moving underwater? Like, it takes me forever just to answer a question or even get out of a chair. And then other times, I'm doing the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together... kind of like I'm trying to shake off a really bad call from work. 

I hope I'm explaining that okay. Does that make sense to you?
Do you feel like your mood changes when you're moving slowly versus when you're pacing around?

Oh, um... I'm actually not entirely sure, to be honest. I hope it's okay to say that. I just... I haven't really noticed a specific shift in how I feel on the inside when I switch between the two. 

I think my mood is mostly just... fine? Or, you know, maybe just a little drained either way, but nothing too extreme. I definitely don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I'm mostly doing okay. 

I'm really sorry, I wish I had a more helpful answer for you. Is that... is it alright if I'm not sure? I just haven't really paid close attention to my mood when it happens.
Do you feel anxious when you're pacing around your apartment and rubbing your hands together?

Anxious? Oh, no, I wouldn't say anxious. I mean, maybe a little bit on edge, like anyone would be after a long day, but definitely not, like, *anxious* anxious. 

I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm, you know, falling apart or anything. It's just a bit of restless energy, I think. Like I just need to walk it off. I don't feel panicked or scared when I do it. It's just... a habit, maybe? 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. Am I explaining that alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever felt persistently sad or empty for a period of time?

Sad or empty? Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? Especially with work and everything, but... no, definitely not persistently sad or anything like that. 

I try to keep a pretty positive outlook, you know? I don't want to be a downer for the people around me. So, no, I wouldn't use words like "sad" or "empty." I'm mostly just... regular, I guess. 

Is that... does that sound like a normal answer? I just want to make sure I'm not, like, missing something important you're looking for.
Do you ever feel irritable?

Irritable? Um... well, maybe just a tiny bit sometimes? But really, no more than anyone else, I promise. 

I mean, dealing with people in customer service all day, you get the occasional rude caller, and... well, it can be a little frustrating. But I never snap at anyone or anything like that. I always try to stay polite and keep things smooth. I really don't like causing friction. 

So, I wouldn't say I'm an irritable person. I mostly just let things roll off my back. I hope that's... I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, angry or difficult to be around. Is that an okay answer?
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or euphoric?

Extremely happy? Or euphoric? Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I have good days, of course! Like when a customer is actually nice, or when I get to relax on the weekend. But... not like, *extremely* happy in a weird way, or out of control or anything. 

I just try to stay pretty even-keeled, you know? I wouldn't want to be one of those people who's just... bouncing off the walls and making everyone else uncomfortable. I'm just a normal amount of happy when good things happen. 

I don't think I've ever had a period like what you're describing. Does that... is that what you were asking? I hope I understood the question right. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture of how I am.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't need much sleep and still felt rested?

Less sleep? Um... no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty good about getting my rest. 

Sometimes if work is busy or I'm stressed about a call, I might toss and turn a little bit, but I definitely need my sleep to function properly. I wouldn't say I ever feel rested if I only get a few hours. I try to make sure I get a solid eight hours so I can be at my best for my shift, you know? I wouldn't want to be groggy and mess up a customer's account.

So, no, I've never had anything like that. I'm a pretty normal sleeper, I think. Is that... does that sound right to you? I hope I'm not overthinking these questions too much.
Have you ever had a period where you felt like you could do a lot more things than you normally can?

Do a lot more things? Like, having a lot of extra energy? Um... no, I don't think so. I'm pretty steady, really. 

I mean, I have my days off where I might catch up on some laundry or run a few errands, but it's nothing out of the ordinary. I just try to keep up with my responsibilities, you know? I wouldn't say I ever feel like I have some kind of superpower to do a million things at once. I usually just stick to my routine so I don't get overwhelmed. 

I really just try to be dependable and consistent, especially for work. I wouldn't want to take on too much and then let anyone down. So... no, I don't think I've experienced that. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I'm trying my best to be helpful.
Do you often feel guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

Guilty? Um... well, I mean, maybe a little bit? But I think everyone feels bad when they mess up, right? 

I just... I want to do a good job. Sometimes I do catch myself kind of replaying small mistakes, you know? Like, if I'm a little slow replying to an email at work, or on one of my side contract jobs. I'll just sit there thinking I let everyone down, and... and that I probably deserve to be fired over it. 

But I know that's probably just me wanting to be a good employee. It's totally normal to want to do your best, isn't it? I just try to be really conscientious so I don't cause any problems for anyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you find it difficult to enjoy activities that you normally like?

Um... well, maybe just a little? I mean, I think it's probably normal to get a little tired of your hobbies sometimes, right? I've been trying to focus on being really dependable at my job, so maybe I'm just a bit drained from that. 

But... yeah, I guess things like sketching, or taking my little coffee notes, or going on weekend hikes... those things used to really make me feel like myself. Lately, though, I'll open up my notebook or lace up my boots, and I just... I kind of feel nothing pulling me toward it. It's just been a little harder to get started. 

I'm sure it's just a temporary phase, though. I definitely plan to get back into it soon so I'm staying active and well-rounded. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the kind of answers you need... I really just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being helpful.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... I know we just touched on this, and I hope it's okay that I'm kind of repeating myself a little. I don't want to waste your time... 

But, yeah, I guess it's like I was saying before. It's just... those things I usually love, like my sketching or writing down my little coffee tasting notes, or even just going for a hike on the weekend... they used to really ground me, you know? They made me feel like me. 

Now, I'll get my notebook out, or I'll put my hiking boots on, and I just... I don't know, I just sit there. There's no spark, or... or nothing pulling me to actually do it. I just feel kind of blank about it all. 

But I'm really trying not to let it get to me, and I'm sure I just need to push through it. Everyone gets in a rut sometimes, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, like you asked. Is that... is that helpful?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? But I think it's pretty normal to fluctuate a little, right? I've just been really focused on work and trying to keep everything running smoothly, so sometimes I just... get a little distracted. 

I guess most days I just sort of forget to eat until late afternoon? And by then, I don't want to make a big mess in the kitchen, so I just grab something easy, like toast or a bowl of cereal. Cooking just feels like a bit too much effort right now, but I'm still eating! 

I did notice my jeans are fitting a little looser than they used to, but I'm sure it's nothing major. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm neglecting myself, because I'm really trying my best.
Do you often worry about things that are unlikely to happen?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I worry all the time, or about everything. I try really hard to just stay focused on the present and do a good job, you know? 

But... I guess there is this one thing. And it probably sounds a little silly, so I hope you don't think I'm completely losing it... but even on weeks where I'm feeling mostly okay, I get this really strong feeling about my old job. They used this specific ticketing software, and... well, I just get so convinced that it's somehow tracking me? Like, through the job sites I look at now. And I worry that it's flagging my name in some system, telling people I'm unreliable or not a good hire. 

I know it sounds like a stretch, and I try to tell myself it's just my mind playing tricks on me because I want to be a good employee so badly. It's just... it feels so real when it happens. But I'm sure it's just normal stress, right? I hope it's okay that I shared that... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm anxious *most* of the time. 

I think I'm generally pretty good at holding things together. Like, at work, I'm usually the one trying to keep the customers calm and make sure everyone's happy. I really try to be positive and helpful. 

I guess I get a little keyed up sometimes, like anyone would, especially when things get busy or if I feel like I'm not doing a good enough job. But it's not this constant, overwhelming thing. I try to just take a deep breath and push through it, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who complains about being stressed all the time. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm anxious all day every day, because I'm really trying my best to stay on top of things.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really hard not to be a worrier, you know? 

I think most of the time, if I'm worrying about something, there's usually a pretty good reason for it. Like, if I'm running late for a shift or if a customer is really upset about something. That's just normal, right? Wanting to do a good job and making sure things go smoothly? 

I really try to just take things one day at a time and not get caught up in all the "what-ifs." I don't want to be someone who just sits around stressing over nothing. I try to stay busy and keep my mind occupied. 

Is that what you mean? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples. I really hope I'm not coming across as someone who just complains or worries over every little thing, because I honestly try my best to just handle whatever comes up.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Um... well, I guess... maybe a little bit? But I'm sure it's just because I've been a bit tired lately, you know? Just regular fatigue.

I used to really love sketching, and I'd always keep these detailed notes on different coffees I tried... and going for weekend hikes was my favorite way to unwind. They always made me feel really grounded, like myself. But... lately, I guess I'll open my sketchbook or go to put on my hiking boots, and... I just don't feel that spark? Like, there's just nothing pulling me toward doing it right now. 

I still try to do them, though! I really do. I know it's important to have hobbies. I just... I don't get that same happy feeling from them at the moment. But I'm sure it'll come back once I catch up on some rest, right? I hope it doesn't make me sound lazy or anything... I really am trying to stay active and do the things I'm supposed to do. Is it normal to go through phases like that?
Do you feel sad most of the time?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm just sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I really try to keep a smile on my face, especially at work. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there has been this sort of... heaviness? Like, most of the time since all this started, there's just been this background feeling of feeling kind of down, and like I mentioned, not really wanting to do my hobbies, and having trouble sleeping... and sometimes feeling bad about myself, like I'm not doing enough. 

It's not always terrible! Some weeks are definitely better and lighter than others, and I really do try to push through it and focus on the positive. I don't want to sound like I'm just wallowing in it, you know? I'm still going to work and trying my best. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things have been going.
Do you feel unhappy most days?

Um... no, not really. I mean, like I said, there's that sort of heaviness sometimes, but I wouldn't use the word "unhappy." 

I try really hard to find the good in every day, you know? Even if I'm a little tired or feeling a bit down, I can usually find something to smile about, especially when I'm helping customers. I really want to be a positive person. I don't want to be someone who just walks around feeling sorry for themselves all the time. 

I'm doing okay, really. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right... I hope I don't sound like I'm contradicting myself from earlier? I just mean that even when things are a little tough, I'm still trying my best to stay upbeat. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you feel like you're depressed?

Um... depressed? I don't... I don't think I'd use that word. That sounds so serious, doesn't it? Like people who can't get out of bed at all or... or who have given up. 

I'm definitely not giving up. I mean, I'm still going to work every day, still trying to be helpful to the customers and be a good employee. I really don't want to come across as someone who's just, you know, depressed and not trying. I'm just going through a bit of a slump, maybe? Just feeling a little off my game lately with the heaviness and being tired. 

I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression. I want to be completely cooperative, I just... I don't think "depressed" is the right label for me. I'm doing my best to keep moving forward. Is it okay that I see it that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
Have you experienced a decrease in interest or pleasure in most activities for at least two weeks?

Um... I wouldn't say a total decrease, no. I mean, I still try to do things! I really do. 

But... well, I guess if I'm being totally honest, things like sketching, or writing down my coffee notes, or going for weekend hikes... they used to make me feel really like myself, you know? But lately, it's just been a little harder to get into them. Like, I'll open my notebook or lace up my boots, and I just... I don't feel that same pull toward it. It's just a little flat right now. 

But I'm sure it's just a phase, right? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing. I'm still trying to stay active and keep busy. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right without sounding too negative.
